transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-13 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair (Redwood); Marta Ruiz, Owen Blake, Samir Patel, Lena Ortiz (Cedar Lane Labs)

Summary:
Quick renewal / expansion check-in. Customer wants to lock a 12- or 24-month renewal with a modest capacity bump and an EU private/onprem pilot (they call it 'edge onramp'). Key security asks (KMS, audit logs, data residency). Need a benchmark in eu-west to validate latency and cost for their 10k qps synthetic scenario.

Topics:
- Renewal term options and stepped pricing
- Dedicated capacity vs hosted burst vs private (VPC / on-prem)
- Security controls: SOC 2 artifacts, KMS/HSM, audit logs, RBAC
- Onramp plan for EU region and staging timing
- Next steps and owners

Action items (briefed above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: okay, hey everyone thanks for joining, um today we wanted to run through the renewal options and the edge onramp plan from Redwood's side. Priya's gonna take the technical parts, I'll cover pricing and timelines. Marta, you had said you wanted this by end of Q1?

[02:00] Marta Ruiz: yeah ideally, um we're trying to align the finance and security reviews so we can commit before the end of march. There's some internal pressure to get EU residency in place for a pilot, so that's one of the drivers.

[04:00] Priya Nair: cool, quick flag — when we talk about EU onramp there are a couple of paths. We can do hosted eu region capacity, Reserved Dedicated in eu-west, or a Private VPC deployment that either runs in customer's cloud or as our on-prem package. Each has different SLA and ops implications.

[06:10] Owen Blake: yeah, so for us the big tradeoffs are latency and data control — we can't send PII out of region, and we also need predictable 99 percentile latency under 150ms for chat flows. Cost is important but reliability and residency beat cheap.

[08:30] Priya Nair: understood. For latency targets we recommend Dedicated pools pinned to your models, with cold/warm cache sizing. We run automatic KV/prefix caching and continuous batching so steady-state token cost is pretty efficient. Slight aside — the KV cache naming in our docs sometimes shows up as K-V cache or kc-cache in older notes, sorry for the inconsistency, that doc's being fixed.

[11:00] Samir Patel: on the security front we need to see SOC2 report, KMS integration details (rotation, HSM option), and example audit logs that show requester identity and model version. How do you expose audit trails from the Redwood Console?

[13:15] Priya Nair: Console exposes per-token trace and per-request metadata. We surface user id, model id, model version, status and execution path. For Private deployments the control plane can be customer-managed; in that case the logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. We'll send a sample log extract — it's in the SOC pack.

[16:00] Alex Chen: on pricing, we can offer a stepped renewal: 12-month at current unit rates with a small uplift for dedicated reserved capacity, or a 24-month with a bigger upfront commit and lower per-token price. We can also include a burst pool for seasonal spikes — that keeps steady-state cheaper. Marta, do you have a preference for term length?

[18:30] Marta Ruiz: I think the team prefers 12 months first with an option to extend if the EU pilot results look good. We need to make sure there's an easy path to add dedicated capacity and to convert to Private in the future without major rework.

[20:45] Owen Blake: also need to understand migration effort. If we kick off a private VPC pilot, how much re-instrumentation is required? Will the SDK calls change?

[22:10] Priya Nair: minimal SDK changes. The API surface is the same — it's the routing and auth that differ. For VPC we provide connector images and a small infra helm chart. For on-prem we ship a slim runtime bundle; there are some ops dependencies (like NV drivers, container runtime) that your infra team will need to allow. We can provide a checklist.

[24:40] Samir Patel: about KMS — we need to know if Redwood supports BYOK with our cloud KMS and if keys can be rotated without downtime. Also HSM-backed key storage would be preferred.

[26:10] Priya Nair: yes, BYOK is supported. Keys can be rotated with minimal disruption — there's a rewrap process; we document it. HSM options are available for Private deployments and through certain partner KMS flows. We'll share the KMS architecture diagram.

[28:30] Alex Chen: re: benchmarks — you shared a 75th/95th latency baseline from the hosted environment, but for the EU pilot Owen asked for 10k synthetic qps to simulate peak chat traffic. We should run that in a staging eu-west cluster, measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec cost. Any constraints on test data?

[30:15] Owen Blake: we'll use synthetic prompts — nothing real/pii — but we want the same token patterns as production: short queries then longer follow-ups with context. We'll send a sample corpus. Also we need a sense of model thumbs — model family, quantization profiles — because we may want a quantized variant for cost.

[32:40] Priya Nair: good point: we can map model variants and quant profiles to cost and latency. The runtime supports int8 quant and some mixed precision flows; some models trade slight accuracy for big cost improvement. We'll include recommended quant profiles per workload. Some of the model names in docs are misspelled sometimes (eg 'redwood-7b-int' shows up as rwd7b-int in older tables) — ignore typos, we'll attach a clean mapping file.

[35:00] Marta Ruiz: what about failover? If eu-west capacity saturates and we failover to a us cluster for short bursts, how do you handle data residency and audits?

[36:30] Priya Nair: we support policy-based routing. For EU-only requests you can set strict residency — then failover will be blocked. Alternatively, you can set a grace failover that routes non-sensitive requests to global capacity. Both are configurable per route in Console or via rollout APIs. We'll walk through policy examples in the next session.

[38:50] Lena Ortiz: procurement question — if we pick the 12-month with burst option, do we need a new contract or is it an amendment? Also any up-front deposit?

[40:05] Alex Chen: typically that's an amendment to the current contract if the legal terms remain the same. For reserved dedicated capacity we ask for a commit and invoice schedule; deposit depends on the package size. I'll draft two documents: amendment (12-month) and a 24-month term SOW for comparison.

[42:20] Samir Patel: quick question — will Redwood rotate model versions automatically when you push a new weights patch? We need traceability for model versioning.

[43:50] Priya Nair: rollouts are explicit — we support canary and A/B. Nothing is auto-switched without a rollout policy. Every request captures model version in the trace. We also retain model artifact IDs in the audit logs.

[45:30] Owen Blake: timeline then: if we decide to pilot private VPC in eu-west, how long to stand up staging?

[46:40] Priya Nair: for a VPC pilot, with Cedar Lane's infra team readiness, typical timeline is 3-4 weeks for staging (helm charts, infra approvals, connector deployment, smoke tests). On-prem is longer — usually 6-8 weeks because of hardware and validations. Dedicated hosted region activation can be done in 2 weeks if capacity is available.

[48:05] Alex Chen: to summarize, action items are: Priya sends SOC2 + KMS diagram + mapping file; Alex sends renewal amendment and pricing options; Owen to send sample load and timing; Samir to send security checklist; Lena to confirm procurement timeline. We'll reconvene after you review the SOC pack and the draft amendment.

[50:10] Marta Ruiz: sounds good. Can we schedule the bench run for week of 2026-02-23? That gives us data to decide by March.

[51:00] Alex Chen: yes we'll aim for that. I'll propose a calendar invite after this call and pin the bench window. Thanks all.

[end] Notes:
